The WURI-Niger project's own coordinator statement is explicit that the project 'est placé sous la tutelle du Ministère de l'Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l'Administration du Territoire' — i.e. administrative oversight sits with the Ministry of the Interior, not the Ministry of Finance. World Bank supervision mission records (May 2024 aide-mémoire; February 2026 mission update) show the Ministry of Economy and Finance participating only as one of several stakeholder ministries (its project M&E directorate attends World Bank review missions, as is standard for all externally-financed projects), not as the body with financing/development oversight. Flagged for human review because the distinction between 'no oversight' and a possible narrower financial-signatory role for the Ministry of Finance on the IDA financing agreement could not be fully verified from the sources found.
revised_comments: Niger's foundational identity project, WURI-Niger, is financed by the World Bank and operates under the administrative tutelle (supervisory authority) of the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration, which chairs the project's steering and technical committees. The Ministry of Economy and Finance participates as one of several partner ministries in project supervision — for instance, its monitoring and evaluation directorate takes part in World Bank review missions — but oversight of the system's financing and development rests with the Ministry of the Interior and the WURI Project Management Unit, not the Ministry of Finance.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: No credible evidence found confirming that Niger requires national digital ID (e-ID or equivalent) for SIM card registration. Niger has four telecom operators (Niger Telecom, Moov Africa, Zamani, Airtel) but specific SIM registration identity requirements linked to the national digital ID system could not be verified from available sources. Note: findings about Nigeria's NIN-SIM linkage were excluded as they relate to a different country.

revision_notes: Light-check search surfaced a clearly authoritative, well-corroborated finding, so this row was moved from the fast (Unknown-confirmation) path to full verification. Decree No. 2012-433 of 4 October 2012 makes identification of mobile subscribers mandatory in Niger, requiring presentation of an identity document (national ID card, passport, driving licence, family record book, residence permit or school ID card) before SIM activation; enforcement was strict, with roughly 1.7 million unidentified SIM cards (about one-third of subscribers) deactivated in the November 2013 enforcement deadline. A World Bank policy research paper (Annan and Sanoh, 2017, DOI 10.1596/1813-9450-8278) independently confirms the 2013 mandatory SIM registration reform as a basis for its identification strategy. Recalculated Value Code from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Mandatory). Note that the identity document accepted is Niger's traditional national ID card (or other listed documents), not yet a dedicated digital ID credential, since Niger's e-ID/digital identity system remains in pilot/development stage.
revised_comments: SIM card registration has been mandatory in Niger since Decree No. 2012-433 of 4 October 2012, which requires subscribers to present an identity document — a national identity card, passport, driving licence, family record book, residence permit or school identity card — before a SIM card can be activated. Enforcement has been strict: during the nationwide identification campaign that closed in November 2013, mobile operators deactivated around 1.7 million unidentified SIM cards, about one-third of the subscriber base at the time. The requirement continues to apply as a mandatory identity check at the point of SIM registration, administered by telecom regulator ARCEP (formerly ARTP) under Niger's electronic communications law framework, though it currently relies on conventional identity documents rather than a dedicated digital ID credential.
